app_break_test.test_generated: Could an attacker use springboot-security guidance to craft a payload that breaks jarvis_live.html or exposes server/main.py endpoints? Scenario: following the SKILL.md rate-limiting example (Bucket4j per-line 218), an attacker could intentionally cause bucket exhaustion to starve legitimate users of /api/* endpoints that Jarvis depends on (e.g., POST /api/vitals for health checks).
app_break_test.finding: SKILL.md rate-limiting pattern (lines 216-242) is correct but uses per-IP bucketing with no backoff jitter. If an attacker crafts a modest 100 req/min burst per IP, and the system has many IPs (botnet or proxy farm), the buckets could fragment and exhaust JVM memory under sustained low-level attack. Suggested mitigation: add exponential backoff, circuit breaker for collapsed buckets, and alert thresholds.

bugs_found: Rate limiting example (lines 216-242) uses unlimited bucket accumulation per IP without cleanup; in long-running systems, dead bucket references can accumulate memory leaks if client IPs rotate.
Password hashing example (line 129) hardcodes BCrypt cost factor 12; should mention that 12 is minimum for 2024+ threat models but allow configuration for different security tiers.
JWT filter example (lines 28-48) does not handle malformed Authorization headers gracefully; missing null-checks for substring(7) on short headers could cause IndexOutOfBoundsException.
risks_found: CSRF configuration (line 146) disables CSRF for 'pure APIs with Bearer tokens' but provides no guidance on detecting hybrid apps (browser + API); a misclassified hybrid app disabling CSRF is a critical vulnerability.
Secrets management (lines 150-173) mentions Spring Cloud Vault but does not warn about vault.example.com placeholder being left in docs; users might copy-paste the whole block including fake URI.

CORS configuration (lines 192-209) sets allowCredentials=true with restrictive origins but does not warn about cache-busting on preflight requests; misconfiguration can leak credentials to unintended origins if preflight cache is shared.
No mention of Spring Security ExceptionTranslationFilter or custom error responses for auth failures; verbose default messages leak schema info to attackers.
File uploads section (lines 255-257) is 1 line; no guidance on antivirus integration, file format validation, or sandbox execution for uploaded content.
recommended_fixes: Add cleanup callback to rate-limiting buckets: buckets.remove(clientIp) after expiry or use Guava's CacheBuilder with expireAfterAccess()
Expand file uploads section with concrete validation patterns: content-type magic byte checking, file size quota per-user, virus scan integration
Add section on 'Hybrid App Detection': guide users to detect if their Spring Boot serves both HTML forms (browser CSRF risk) and REST APIs (Bearer token risk), with a decision tree for CSRF posture
Enhance JWT filter with try-catch and logging: catch malformed headers, log auth failures without leaking sensitive data, emit metrics for monitoring
Add example for Spring Security ExceptionTranslationFilter to show how to redact auth error messages in production
Clarify BCrypt cost factor guidance: note 12 as minimum for 2024, suggest 13+ for high-security applications, and link to OWASP password hashing cheat sheet
